candidate.answerReason: Equal squares have equal or opposite bases. The two resulting linear equations give 4 and 2/3, matching the unordered key.

methods.label: Use equal or opposite bases
methods.explanation: Taking square roots on both sides gives \(2x-3=x+1\) or \(2x-3=-(x+1)\). The former gives \(x=4\); the latter gives \(3x=2\), so \(x=2/3\). Alternatively, move terms and factor using the difference of squares.
methods.levelReason: Uses Grade 7 square-root facts and linear equations.

methods.label: Factor a difference of squares
methods.explanation:
Subtract the squared expressions so that the difference-of-squares identity produces linear factors:
\[
\begin{aligned}
(2x-3)^2-(x+1)^2&=0,\\
[(2x-3)-(x+1)][(2x-3)+(x+1)]&=0,\\
(x-4)(3x-2)&=0.
\end{aligned}
\]
A product is zero if and only if at least one factor is zero. Thus \(x-4=0\) or \(3x-2=0\), giving the two roots \(4,\,2/3\).
methods.levelReason: Uses the Grade 8 difference-of-squares identity and Grade 9 factoring method.
